ABS Wheel Speed Sensor

This section lists the hub-mounted sensors that report wheel speed to the ABS module. Typical signs include an ABS or traction light, a speedometer that drops out, or a code for one corner. Clean the tone ring and connector before condemning the sensor — packed debris mimics an open circuit.

47 parts here are engine-specific — pick your engine above to filter the table. Parts are split into Economy (value-priced) and Standard Replacement (OE-spec).

Brake Bleeder Screw

This section lists the bleeders used to purge air from the hydraulic circuit. Typical signs include a rounded head, a seeping bleeder, or a fastener that will not hold torque. Do not force a new screw into a stripped hole — repair the thread first.

Brake Fluid

This section lists the hydraulic fluid listed for this vehicle's brake system. Typical signs include a soft pedal, fluid that tests high for water, or a reservoir that has gone dark. Use only the DOT grade in the notes — mixing DOT 5 silicone with glycol fluid ruins the hydraulic system.

Parts are split into DOT 3 (DOT 3 brake-fluid spec), DOT 4 (DOT 4 brake-fluid spec) and MULTI-USE (multi-use fluid).

Brake Hose

This section lists the flexible lines that carry brake fluid to each caliper. Typical signs include a spongy pedal, a bulge in the hose, or a wet fitting after a hard stop. Replace hoses in pairs on an axle; a hose that looks fine can still collapse internally.

26 parts here are engine-specific — pick your engine above to filter the table. Parts are split into Economy (value-priced) and Standard Replacement (OE-spec).

Caliper

This section lists the hydraulic clamps that squeeze the pads onto the rotor. Typical signs include a vehicle that pulls to one side, a pad worn to the backing on one piston only, or a hose that weeps at the caliper banjo. Hang the caliper from the spring — never by the hose — and replace slide pins or boots that are dry or torn.

Disc Brake Hardware Kit

This section lists the abutment clips, springs and pins that hold disc pads in the caliper. Install new abutment clips and slides with every pad job; reused hardware is the usual source of noise.

Rotor & Brake Pad Kit

This section lists matched rotor-and-pad kits sold as a set for one axle or wheel. Typical signs include the same squeal, grind or shudder that sends pads and rotors to the scrap pile together. A matched kit keeps friction and iron on the same axle; finish both sides before driving.

117 parts here are engine-specific — pick your engine above to filter the table. Parts are split into Daily Driver (everyday commuting duty), Economy (value-priced), Fully Coated (Maximum Protection For Rust Prone Areas), Heavy Duty (Long Life, Truck & Tow), and 3 other catalog groups.

How to read these tables

Each table row is one part for this vehicle. Use the columns and badges below so you order the right number — not a look-alike for another engine, market, or grade.

Market badges (US, CA, MX)

The Markets column shows where that part’s fitment was published — the country where the vehicle was first sold, not where the part was manufactured.

  • 🇺🇸 US United States — vehicles first sold in the United States.
  • 🇨🇦 CA Canada — vehicles first sold in Canada.
  • 🇲🇽 MX Mexico — vehicles first sold in Mexico.

A row can show more than one badge when the same part number is listed for multiple markets. If only one badge appears, that is all the source catalog published for that number — still confirm notes and your vehicle’s market if you are unsure.

Popular badge

Popular marks parts the catalog flags as commonly applied to this vehicle. It is a demand signal, not a quality or safety rating.

Economy, Standard, Premium, and similar headers

When a part type splits into groups like Economy or Standard Replacement, those are catalog sales grades for how the part is sold — not different vehicles. Pick the grade that matches how you drive; the notes column still carries position and fit details.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many brake & wheel hub parts fit the 2021 Honda Civic?

660 brake & wheel hub parts fit the 2021 Honda Civic across 3 engines on AutoFactsDB.com.

Do brake & wheel hub parts differ between the 2021 Honda Civic engines?

Some do. For the 2021 Honda Civic, 91 parts fit every engine (1.5L L4 Turbo, 2.0L L4 and 2.0L L4 Turbo) and 569 parts are engine-specific. Match your engine first.

What do the US, CA and MX badges mean on 2021 Honda Civic parts?

They mark the country where the vehicle was first sold — United States, Canada or Mexico — not where the part was made. A row can show more than one badge when the same part number is published for multiple markets.

Which brands supply brake & wheel hub parts for the 2021 Honda Civic?

Dynamic Friction, Power Stop and R1 Concepts supply brake & wheel hub parts for the 2021 Honda Civic, among 54 brands listed.

What brake & wheel hub types are listed for the 2021 Honda Civic?

The largest brake & wheel hub types for the 2021 Honda Civic are brake pad, rotor & brake pad kit and rotor.
